newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-HISTORY OF BUBKA'S FIVE WORLD POLE VAULT TITLES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HISTORY OF BUBKA'S FIVE WORLD POLE VAULT TITLES.

text.p: Pole vaulter Sergei Bubka of Ukraine is the only athlete to win five consecutive world titles.
Here is a chronology of his victories since the first world championships in 1983.

1983 Helsinki - The turning point in Bubka's career came at the Olympic Stadium on August 14, 1993 when he won the first world championship with a clearance of 5.70 metres. Jumping in the red vest of the Soviet Union and distinctive striped socks, Bubka kept his composure for almost seven hours. The previous day's qualifying competition was abandoned because of heavy rain and high winds and 27 men took part in the final. Konstantin Volkov of the Soviet Union took the silver (5.60) and Atanas Tarev of Bulgaria the bronze (5.60).

1987 Rome - Bubka had improved the world record seven times, from 5.85 to 6.03 metres between Helsinki and Rome, and there was little doubt he would retain his title which he duly did do on September 5, 1987. He needed only two jumps to do so, coming in at 5.70, his winning height in 1983, and returning at 5.85, good enough for the title in Rome's Olympic Stadium. Thierry Vigneron of France took the silver (5.80) and Radion Gataullin, like Bubka, representing the Soviet Union, the bronze (5.80).

1991 Tokyo - With the Olympic title secured in Seoul three years earlier, Bubka returned to Asia looking for his third world title triumphed after a thrilling battle with Istvan Bagyula of Hungary on August 29. This was Bubka's toughest battle to date and there were several heart-stopping moments for his fans before he won with his final clearance of 5.95 metres. If he had failed with that jump, he would have finished seventh. Bagyula took the silver with his 5.90 clearance, while Maksim Tarasov, of the Soviet Union, clinched the bronze (5.85), a year before his Olympic victory in Barcelona.

1993 Stuttgart - A gold medal for Ukraine rather than the Soviet Union marked Bubka's fourth victory on August 19, 1993 which was significant for two other reasons. It meant he was the only athlete to have won his event in all four championships so far contested and his 6.00 metres victory clearance was the first successful vault of that height in a major championship. The medals went to four men who were once all team mates for the Soviet Union but were now wearing vests of their newly independent nations. Grigory Yegorov of Kazakhstan took the silver (5.90), while Tarasov, now of Russia, and Igor Trandenkov, also of Russia, finished joint third (5.80).

1995 Gothenburg - Despite winning his fifth successive title on August 9, 1995, Bubka was annoyed with himself for failing to crown his achievment with a world record of 6.15. After winning the competition with a clearance of 5.92, Bubka failed to raise his world record from 6.14 admitting afterwards he should have changed his run-up which he failed to do. Tarasov took the silver (5.86) and Jean Galfione of France -- destined to win the Olympic gold in Atlanta the following year -- took the bronze (5.86).
